question.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=k{x}^{2}+3x-15$ is $x=4.$ Find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, we will set our result equal to $4.$ 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=k$ and $b=3$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{3}{2(k)} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2k}.\end{aligned}
$$

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=4,$ so we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2k} & =4 \\ -3 & =8k \\ k & =-\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
